Python Modules Documentation

Introduction

The application is divided into multiple Python modules. Each module handles a specific responsibility to keep the code organized and maintainable.

Module Dependency Diagram

        flowchart LR
    main[main.py] --> auth[auth.py]
    main --> access[access.py]
    main --> db[db.py]
    auth --> db
    auth --> security[security.py]
    access --> db
    auth --> utils[utils.py]
    access --> utils

main.py

The main.py module is the entry point of the FastAPI application.

Responsibilities:

  • Create the FastAPI application instance.

  • Initialize the database.

  • Configure SessionMiddleware.

  • Mount static files.

  • Register authentication and page routers.

  • Configure application exception handling.

Example usage

# Run the application from the project root
#   uvicorn app.main:app --reload

from fastapi import FastAPI
from starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware

app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key="change-this-secret")

API reference

Main module for the User Access Control application.

This module initializes and configures the FastAPI application, loads environment variables, sets up session management, serves static files, and registers application routers.

Application Setup:

  1. Loads environment variables from the .env file using load_dotenv().

  2. Imports authentication and access-control routers.

  3. Creates a FastAPI application instance.

  4. Adds SessionMiddleware to manage user sessions securely.

  5. Mounts the static directory to serve CSS, JavaScript, and other static files.

  6. Registers the authentication and access-control routers.

Environment Variables:
SECRET_KEY (str): Secret key used by SessionMiddleware to sign

session cookies. Uses a development default if not configured.

Modules:

auth: Handles login, logout, and home page functionality. access: Handles page1-page4 routes and user access permissions. utils: Provides BASE_DIR for locating application resources.

Static Files:

URL: /static Directory: BASE_DIR/static

Application:

app: The main FastAPI application instance.

auth.py

The auth.py module handles authentication-related routes.

Responsibilities:

  • Process user login requests.

  • Verify user credentials.

  • Create user sessions after successful login.

  • Handle logout requests.

  • Clear user sessions.

Example usage

# POST /login  (form fields: username, password)
#
# Valid credentials   -> user ID stored in session, redirect to home page
# Invalid credentials -> login.html shown again with an error message
#
# GET /logout
#
# Session cleared -> redirect to login page

API reference

Authentication module for the User Access Control application.

This module defines the authentication API router and imports the functions required to handle user login, logout, session management, and home page functionality.

It uses FastAPI form handling, database queries, password verification, and session-based authentication to manage user access.

Imports:

escape: Escapes special HTML characters to help prevent HTML injection. APIRouter: Creates a router for registering authentication endpoints. Request: Provides access to request data and session information. Form: Extracts form data submitted by users. HTMLResponse: Returns HTML content as an HTTP response. RedirectResponse: Redirects users to another URL. Response: Base response class for HTML and redirect responses. get_user_by_username: Retrieves a user record using their username. verify_password: Checks the entered password against the stored hash. load_html: Loads HTML templates from the application’s HTML directory. current_user: Retrieves the currently logged-in user’s database record. get_user_pages: Retrieves the pages assigned to a user.

Global Variables:

router (APIRouter): Router used to register authentication endpoints.

Authentication Features:

  • User login and password verification.

  • Session management after successful login.

  • Logout and session clearing.

  • Home page access for authenticated users.

  • Retrieving user-specific page permissions.

app.auth.home(request: Request) → Response[source]

Display the home page with the logged-in user’s details and assigned page links.

Parameters:

request (Request) – Incoming HTTP request object. Used to identify the currently logged-in user and access session information.

What it does:

  1. Handles GET requests to the “/home” URL.

  2. Checks whether the user is logged in using current_user().

  3. If the user is not logged in, redirects them to “/login”.

  4. Retrieves the list of pages assigned to the user using get_user_pages().

  5. If the user has assigned pages: - Generates HTML list items containing links to each page. - Replaces “page” in page names with “Page “ for display.

  6. If no pages are assigned, displays a message: “No pages assigned to you yet.”

  7. Loads the home.html template.

  8. Replaces the “__NAME__” placeholder with the user’s escaped full name.

  9. Replaces the “__LINKS__” placeholder with the generated page links or the no-pages message.

  10. Returns the updated home page as an HTML response.

Returns:

RedirectResponse: Redirects unauthenticated users

to “/login” with status code 303.

HTMLResponse: Displays the home page with the user’s

name and assigned page links.

Return type:

Response

Example

Logged-in user with assigned pages:

Displays the home page with the user’s name and available page links.

Logged-in user without assigned pages:

Displays “No pages assigned to you yet.”

Unauthenticated user:

Redirects to “/login”.

app.auth.login(request: Request, username: str = Form(PydanticUndefined), password: str = Form(PydanticUndefined)) → Response[source]

Authenticate a user using their username and password.

Parameters:

  • request (Request) – Incoming HTTP request object. Used to access and manage the user session.

  • username (str) – Username entered in the login form. Required form field.

  • password (str) – Password entered in the login form. Required form field.

What it does:

  1. Receives the username and password submitted through the login form.

  2. Removes leading and trailing whitespace from the username.

  3. Fetches the user details from the database using get_user_by_username().

  4. Checks whether the user exists.

  5. Verifies the entered password against the stored password hash using verify_password().

  6. If the username or password is incorrect: - Displays an error message. - Returns the login page with HTTP status code 401.

  7. If authentication is successful: - Clears the existing session. - Stores the user’s ID in the session. - Redirects the user to the home page.

Returns:

HTMLResponse: Returns the login page with an error

message if authentication fails.

RedirectResponse: Redirects the authenticated user

to “/home” with HTTP status code 303.

Return type:

HTMLResponse | RedirectResponse

Example

Input:

username = “admin” password = “admin123”

Successful login:

Redirects to “/home”.

Failed login:

Displays “Wrong username or password.” and returns HTTP 401.

app.auth.login_form() → HTMLResponse[source]

Display the login page to the user.

Parameters:

None – This function does not require any input parameters.

What it does:

  1. Handles GET requests to the “/login” URL.

  2. Loads the login.html file.

  3. Replaces the “__ERROR__” placeholder with an empty string. This ensures that no error message is displayed initially.

  4. Returns the updated HTML content as a response.

Returns:

Returns the login page HTML content

with the error message placeholder cleared.

Return type:

HTMLResponse

Example

Request:

GET /login

Output:

Displays the login page without an error message.

app.auth.logout(request: Request) → RedirectResponse[source]

Log out the currently authenticated user.

Parameters:

request (Request) – Incoming HTTP request object. Used to access and manage the user’s session.

What it does:

  1. Handles GET requests to the “/logout” URL.

  2. Clears all data stored in the user’s session.

  3. Removes the user’s login information from the session.

  4. Redirects the user to the login page.

  5. Uses HTTP status code 303 for redirection.

Returns:

Redirects the user to “/login”

after clearing the session.

Return type:

RedirectResponse

Example

Request:

GET /logout

Output:

Clears the user session and redirects to “/login”.

app.auth.root(request: Request) → RedirectResponse[source]

Handle requests to the root URL (“/”) and redirect users based on their login status.

Parameters:

request (Request) – Incoming HTTP request object. Contains the user’s session information.

What it does:

  1. Receives a request when the user visits the root URL.

  2. Checks whether the user’s session contains a “user_id”.

  3. If user_id exists, redirects the user to “/home”.

  4. If user_id does not exist, redirects the user to “/login”.

  5. Uses HTTP status code 303 to perform the redirect.

Returns:

Redirects the user to either:

  • ”/home” if the user is logged in.

  • ”/login” if the user is not logged in.

Return type:

RedirectResponse

Example

Logged-in user:

GET / Redirects to /home

Not logged-in user:

GET / Redirects to /login

access.py

The access.py module handles page-level authorization.

Responsibilities:

  • Define or retrieve user page permissions.

  • Check whether a user can access a requested page.

  • Protect restricted pages.

  • Handle unauthorized access.

Example usage

from app.access import check_page_access

if check_page_access(username="priti", page="page1"):
    print("Show page1.html")      # Priti has page1 permission
else:
    print("Show denied.html")

check_page_access("priti", "page3")   # False -> denied.html
check_page_access("admin", "page3")   # True  -> page3.html

API reference

Access Control module for the User Access Control application.

This module defines the API router and configuration required to manage protected pages and control user access based on assigned permissions.

It uses FastAPI routing, database connections, session-based authentication, and HTML response handling to provide authorized access to application pages.

Imports:

escape: Escapes special HTML characters to help prevent HTML injection. APIRouter: Creates a router for registering application endpoints. Request: Provides access to request and session information. HTMLResponse: Returns HTML content as an HTTP response. RedirectResponse: Redirects users to another URL. get_connection: Establishes a connection to the MySQL database. load_html: Loads HTML files from the application’s HTML directory. current_user: Retrieves the currently authenticated user. Callable: Represents a function that can be called. Response: Base response class for HTML and redirect responses.

Global Variables:

router (APIRouter): Router used to register access-control endpoints. PAGES (list[str]): List of protected page names managed by this module.

Protected Pages:

page1, page2, page3, page4

app.access.get_user_pages(user_id)[source]

Get all pages that a specific user is allowed to access.

Parameters:

user_id (int or str) – Unique ID of the user.

What it does:

  1. Connects to the database.

  2. Fetches all page names assigned to the given user_id from the user_pages table.

  3. Sorts the page names alphabetically.

  4. Closes the database connection.

Returns:

A list of page names assigned to the user.

Returns an empty list if no pages are assigned.

Return type:

list[str]

Example

Input:

get_user_pages(101)

Output:

[‘Attendance’, ‘Dashboard’, ‘Employee’]

app.access.make_page_route(page_name: str) → Callable[[Request], Response][source]

Create a page route handler with authentication and authorization checks.

Parameters:

page_name (str) – Name of the HTML page to access. Example: “page1”, “page2”, “dashboard”.

What it does:

  1. Creates an inner function named page_view().

  2. Checks whether the user is logged in.

  3. Redirects unauthenticated users to the login page.

  4. Checks whether the requested page is assigned to the logged-in user.

  5. If access is denied, displays the denied.html page.

  6. If access is allowed, displays the requested HTML page.

Returns:

Returns a page_view function that accepts an HTTP Request and returns an HTTP Response.

Return type:

Callable[[Request], Response]

Example

make_page_route(“page1”)

Returns a page handler for page1.

db.py

The db.py module handles database operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Connect to the MySQL database.

  • Retrieve user records.

  • Retrieve user permissions.

  • Perform database-related operations.

Example usage

from app.db import get_connection

conn = get_connection()
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = %s", ("priti",))
print(cursor.fetchone())
conn.close()

API reference

Database configuration module for the User Access Control application.

This module imports the required libraries and loads environment variables used for connecting to the MySQL database.

Imports:
os: Provides functions to access environment variables and

handle operating system paths.

pymysql: Provides MySQL database connectivity and query execution. load_dotenv: Loads database configuration variables from a .env file.

Configuration:

load_dotenv(): Loads environment variables from the .env file into the application’s environment.

Purpose:

Provides the database configuration required by other modules to establish MySQL database connections.

app.db.get_connection()[source]

Create and return a connection to the MySQL database.

Reads the database configuration from environment variables:

DB_HOST: Database server hostname (default: localhost). DB_PORT: Database server port (default: 3306). DB_USER: Database username (default: root). DB_PASSWORD: Database password. DB_NAME: Database name (default: access_demo).

Uses DictCursor so query results are returned as dictionaries, allowing columns to be accessed by their names.

Returns:

An active MySQL database connection.

Return type:

pymysql.connections.Connection

Raises:

  • pymysql.MySQLError – If the database connection cannot be established.

  • ValueError – If DB_PORT contains an invalid integer value.

Example

conn = get_connection() cursor = conn.cursor() cursor.execute(“SELECT * FROM users”) users = cursor.fetchall() conn.close()

app.db.get_user_by_id(user_id)[source]

Retrieve a user record from the database using their user ID.

Establishes a database connection, executes a parameterized SQL query to find the user with the specified ID, and fetches the matching record.

Parameters:

user_id (int) – The unique ID of the user to retrieve.

Returns:

A dictionary containing the user’s database record if a matching user is found; otherwise, None.

Return type:

dict | None

Raises:

pymysql.MySQLError – If a database operation fails.

Example

user = get_user_by_id(1)

if user:

print(user[“username”])

else:

print(“User not found.”)

app.db.get_user_by_username(username)[source]

Retrieve a user record from the database using their username.

Establishes a database connection, executes a parameterized SQL query to find the matching user, and fetches the first matching record.

Parameters:

username (str) – The username of the user to search for.

Returns:

A dictionary containing the user’s database record if a matching user is found; otherwise, None.

Return type:

dict | None

Raises:

pymysql.MySQLError – If a database operation fails.

Example

user = get_user_by_username(“admin”)

if user:

print(user[“username”])

else:

print(“User not found.”)

security.py

The security.py module handles password security.

Responsibilities:

  • Generate password hashes using bcrypt.

  • Verify passwords against stored hashes.

Example usage

from app.security import hash_password, verify_password

hashed = hash_password("MySecret@123")
print(verify_password("MySecret@123", hashed))   # True
print(verify_password("wrong", hashed))          # False

API reference

app.security.hash_password(plain_password: str) → str[source]

Hash a plain-text password using the bcrypt hashing algorithm.

Encodes the password into UTF-8 bytes, generates a random salt, and creates a secure password hash using bcrypt.

Parameters:

plain_password (str) – The original plain-text password to hash.

Returns:

The bcrypt password hash decoded as a UTF-8 string.

Return type:

str

Example

hashed = hash_password(“admin123”) print(hashed)

app.security.verify_password(plain_password: str, password_hash: str) → bool[source]

Verify a plain-text password against an existing bcrypt password hash.

Encodes the provided password and stored hash into UTF-8 bytes, then uses bcrypt to check whether the password matches the hash.

Parameters:

  • plain_password (str) – The plain-text password entered by the user.

  • password_hash (str) – The previously stored bcrypt password hash.

Returns:

True if the password matches the stored hash;

otherwise, False.

Return type:

bool

Example

hashed = hash_password(“admin123”) is_valid = verify_password(“admin123”, hashed) print(is_valid) # True

utils.py

The utils.py module contains reusable helper functions.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide common utility functionality.

  • Avoid repeating shared logic across application modules.

Example usage

from app.utils import some_helper

result = some_helper("input value")

API reference

Utility functions for the User Access Control application.

This module provides common helper functions for locating application resources, loading HTML templates, and retrieving the currently authenticated user from the session.

app.utils.current_user(request: Request)[source]

Retrieve the currently logged-in user’s database record.

Reads the user_id from the request session and uses get_user_by_id() to retrieve the corresponding user record from the database.

The login function (Member A) stores the user’s ID in the session after successful authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The incoming FastAPI request containing the user’s session information.

Returns:

The logged-in user’s database record if a valid user_id exists in the session; otherwise, None.

Return type:

dict | None

Example

user = current_user(request)

if user:

print(user[“username”])

else:

print(“User is not logged in.”)

app.utils.load_html(file_name: str) → str[source]

Read and return the contents of an HTML file from the app/html directory.

Constructs the file path using BASE_DIR, opens the specified HTML file with UTF-8 encoding, and reads its contents.

Parameters:

file_name (str) – Name of the HTML file to read.

Returns:

Contents of the HTML file as a string.

Return type:

str

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If the specified HTML file does not exist.

  • OSError – If an error occurs while opening or reading the file.

Example

html = load_html(“login.html”)

HTML Templates

The application uses HTML templates to display its user interface.

login.html

Displays the login form.

home.html

Displays the home page after successful login.

denied.html

Displays an access denied message.

page1.html to page4.html

These are protected pages displayed according to user permissions.

Static Files

The static directory contains CSS files used to style the application’s HTML pages.

Conclusion

Separating responsibilities into different modules improves readability, maintainability, and code reuse.
